newsitem.title: USA: Westmoreland Coal files for bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Westmoreland Coal files for bankruptcy.

text.p: Westmoreland Coal Co. said on Monday it filed a Chapter 11 bankruptcy petition after talks to restructure $160 million in retiree benefit obligations broke down.

The company, which recently moved its headquarters to Colorado from Philadelphia, said it was forced to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection because of the dispute over $160 million with the United Mine Workers of America pension and benefit funds.
Union representatives were not immediately available for comment.
The company said talks, which have gone on for 14 months, to settle the dispute broke down Monday morning.

"Westmoreland is trying to serve obligations, not escape them. We do not dispute our obligation to provide 100 percent lifetime health benefits to UMWA retirees under the Federal Coal Act passed in 1992," Chairman Christopher Seglem said.
But the company said it was looking for a way to live up to the obligation without liquidating the 142-year-old company. It said its best value was as an on-going entity.
Westmoreland said it pays more than $14 million a year to the mine workers coal fund and that its supports beneficiaries who never worked for Westmoreland nor its subsidiaries.
The Coal Act created a so-called "last man's club" among coal producers, meaning Westmoreland is obligated to pay for employees who worked for coal companies now out of business.
